root_cause: Overlapping rebalance calls can complete out of order. The code replaces the active partition set with any response, including one from an older generation, rather than rejecting stale assignments.
bug_location: rebalance: the assignment is applied after the asynchronous fetch without checking its generation
observed_risk: The consumer can retain a stale partition assignment while another member owns those partitions, causing duplicate processing or inconsistent group state.
failure_scenario: A rebalance for generation 1 starts and its assignment response is delayed. A second rebalance for generation 2 completes and installs its assignment. The delayed generation 1 response then arrives and overwrites the active partition set.
expected_behavior: Apply an assignment only if its generation is still current. A response from an older rebalance must not overwrite the active assignment.
validation_checks: Delay the generation 1 assignment response until after generation 2 has been applied, then verify that the active assignment remains at generation 2.
Verify that stale assignment responses are ignored and do not replace the current partition set.
Exercise overlapping rebalance calls and confirm that ownership reflects only the latest accepted generation.

root_cause: The consumer advances the committed offset before the record has been processed successfully. A successful commit makes the record eligible to be skipped after a restart, even if handling never completed.
bug_location: processRecord: the commit call occurs before the call to handle
observed_risk: Records can be permanently skipped when processing fails after the offset commit.
failure_scenario: The consumer receives a record, commits its next offset, and then the process stops or handle rejects before completing. On restart, consumption resumes after that record.
expected_behavior: Commit the next offset only after handling succeeds, so restart recovery can replay any record whose processing did not complete.
validation_checks: Make handle reject and verify that the committed offset does not advance past the record.
Stop the consumer after commit but before handling and verify that the test reproduces a skipped record.
Verify that a successful handler completion is followed by a commit of exactly the next offset.

root_cause: Records from the same partition are processed concurrently, and each completion commits its own next offset. A later record can therefore advance the partition's committed offset beyond an earlier record that is still being processed.
bug_location: processBatch: concurrent per-record handlers commit offsets independently
observed_risk: An unfinished earlier record can be skipped after a restart because a later completion advanced the committed offset past it.
failure_scenario: Two records from one partition are processed concurrently. The later record finishes first and commits its next offset; the consumer then stops before the earlier record finishes. Recovery starts after the later record's offset.
expected_behavior: For each partition, commit only the next offset in the contiguous sequence of successfully processed records. Concurrent processing must not allow a later completion to move the committed position past unfinished work.
validation_checks: Use controlled promises to make the later record finish before the earlier record and inspect the committed offset.
Stop processing after the later record commits but before the earlier handler completes, then verify whether recovery skips the earlier record.
Verify that a per-partition commit frontier advances only when all preceding records have completed successfully.
